rounds.verdict: Do not publish: the barbell tears away from the lifter's hands as the layers scale, ruining the lockout and the final frame.
filmIssues: The lifter and barbell do not stay together: because each layer scales about its own centre, the barbell visibly separates and enlarges away from the lifter's hands in the second half — by t=0.6-1.0 the bar drops across his head/neck and the plates drift outward, breaking the lockout hold.
Apart from that faulty layer scale, the move is essentially a plain centred push-in with a very small rise, so it is no better than the baseline and does not clearly express the triumph.
The final frame is not a good dwell image because the detached, oversized barbell is the most noticeable element.

plan.rationale: A triumph at lockout: the lifter and his held barbell rise and grow as one while the camera tilts up and closes in, lifting the 1958 gold-medal hold toward the arena lamps.

rounds.verdict: Coherent and publishable-looking, but no better than a plain centred push-in on the same plate, and the final frame over-crops the platform.
filmIssues: The film is essentially a plain centred push-in: the lifter and barbell only grow and drift slightly upward together, so it adds no narrative movement beyond the baseline it is scored against.

The final zoom of 1.36 is too tight for a dwell frame — at t=1 the platform's base is cropped by the bottom edge and the lifter's feet sit awkwardly close to the frame edge, losing the grounded arena composition.
No tearing, doubled edges or ghosting is visible: lifter and barbell share depth and drift, so the hand-to-bar join stays intact throughout.
The light-sweep is subtle and fitting for the arena lamps, and the 1950s offset-lithograph style is preserved.

plan.rationale: A triumph at lockout, fixed and bolder: lifter and barbell receive identical depth, identical upward drift and no independent layer scaling, so they translate and grow only together through camera parallax and preserve the hand-to-bar join. A stronger push-in from the full arena to the held lift, rising toward the lamps, makes the gold-medal hold the clear final dwell image.

filmIssues: The t=0 opening frame is an empty platform: the rise entrance hides the weightlifter and barbell, the subject of the scene, so the page opens without its hero.
Once the lifter appears the rise plus push-in does read as a triumph, and cut-1/cut-2 stay locked together with no visible tearing, doubled edges or ghost at the hand-to-bar join.
The final frame is a strong hold — lifter large, centred, bar overhead, platform and feet in frame — but the opening failure and the entrance pop keep it below publishable.
Light-sweep is fitting and subtle for the 1950s lithograph style, which is otherwise preserved.
